task.description: Measured 2026-11-10 while reminting every member store (GB-347). Plan blueprints and the tickets that name them are not checked against each other, so a store can hold a plan nobody owns and a ticket can point at a file that does not exist - and no command says so.  chalkline: plans/GB-18.md has no owning ticket (no GB-18 in that store); CH-1 and CH-2 report plan_file_path .gaugeblock/storypole/plans/CH-1.md and CH-2.md, and neither file exists. The pointers were dangling before the remint as CH-1.md and CH-2.md and are still dangling after it.  benchwork: plans/GB-17.md and plans/GB-46.md have no owning ticket.  storypole: plans/GB-36.md has no owning ticket.  remint cannot fix this by design - it renames a blueprint when a ticket owns the key, and there is nothing to rename an orphan after - so the orphans survive a migration that is otherwise exhaustive. The check that would catch it is cheap: for every store, name each plan file with no owning ticket and each plan_file_path that resolves to nothing. `ledger-verify` is the natural home, alongside the structural ledger checks it already performs.
task.title: plan blueprints can be orphaned or point at files that do not exist, and no command notices

events.description:
Measured 2026-11-10 while reminting every member store (GB-347). Plan blueprints and the tickets that name them are not checked against each other, so a store can hold a plan nobody owns and a ticket can point at a file that does not exist - and no command says so.  chalkline: plans/GB-18.md has no owning ticket (no GB-18 in that store); CH-1 and CH-2 report plan_file_path .gaugeblock/storypole/plans/CH-1.md and CH-2.md, and neither file exists. The pointers were dangling before the remint as CH-1.md and CH-2.md and are still dangling after it.  benchwork: plans/GB-17.md and plans/GB-46.md have no owning ticket.  storypole: plans/GB-36.md has no owning ticket.  remint cannot fix this by design - it renames a blueprint when a ticket owns the key, and there is nothing to rename an orphan after - so the orphans survive a migration that is otherwise exhaustive. The check that would catch it is cheap: for every store, name each plan file with no owning ticket and each plan_file_path that resolves to nothing. `ledger-verify` is the natural home, alongside the structural ledger checks it already performs.

CHECK IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-10, AND IT FOUND MORE THAN THIS TICKET ASSUMED.

`storypole ledger-verify` now audits plans against tickets as well as ledgers against replays:
  orphan    <store>/plans/<KEY>.md has no owning ticket
  dangling  <store>/<TICKET> -> plans/<KEY>.md, where that file does not exist

MEASURED on the suite after the remint:
  59 orphan blueprints, 50 dangling pointers.
  46 of the orphans sit in the ROOT store's plans directory, named for GB-* keys that are now member tickets
  (plans/OF-20.md, OF-26.md, BW-16.md ...). The dangling pointers are the other end of the same files:
  a member ticket pointing at `.gaugeblock/storypole/plans/<KEY>.md` inside ITS OWN repository.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is not the remint. Blueprints were written to the canonical root plans directory while the
tickets were distributed into members, and the pointer was written repository-relative, so it never resolved in
the member that owns the ticket. Verified rather than assumed: outfeed OF-26 pointed at plans/OF-26.md before
the remint and that file did not exist in outfeed then either; the same holds for OF-8, OF-9, SH-4 and RB-4.

THE REMEDY IS EXACT. Using the remint record, every member-side dangling pointer resolves to a blueprint in the root
plans directory under the ticket's PRE-REMINT key: 47 checked, 47 matched, 0 unmatched.
  benchwork BW-16 -> plans/BW-16.md exists at the root, so the file belongs at benchwork/plans/BW-16.md
Moving each blueprint to its owner and naming it for the ticket's current key would clear both sides at once - the
orphan disappears because the file left, and the dangling pointer becomes valid because the file arrived where the
pointer already looks. That is a write pass, so it needs a verb with a dry run, the same as every other migration
here; it is not implemented in this change.

NOT GATED, DELIBERATELY. `ledger-verify` reports these and does not fail on them. Resolving is a decision - move the
blueprint, or clear a pointer whose document is already inline in the ticket as `design_markdown` - and a check that
guessed would be worse than one that asks. It also must not block eleven repositories' verification chains on data
nobody has judged yet. The findings are in `--json` under `plans` for anything that wants to gate on them later.

Tests: an orphan blueprint and a dangling pointer are both reported; a plan file that exists is clean.
